description: Somos NEXO, un equipo enfocado en tecnología, innovación y creación de soluciones con impacto real. Nos interesan la programación, IA, datos y resolución de problemas. Buscamos personas curiosas, comprometidas y colaborativas, con habilidades en desarrollo, IA, análisis de datos, UX/UI, investigación, comunicación o áreas afines. No importa si eres experto: buscamos ganas de aprender, aportar y construir juntos.
summary: Global atlases like NASA Mars Trek were built for orbital views rather than the hyperlocalized areas astronauts target during individual Marswalks. NEXO-ARES (Astronaut Routing & EVA Survival System) solves the Martian Map challenge by transforming multi-mission NASA and ESA datasets into an active, offline-first survival copilot hyperlocalized to Jezero Crater. Combining a habitat route-planning console with a hands-free 360° Helmet Visor HUD, NEXO-ARES helps explorers execute safe surface excursions while conducting high-value astrobiology. Its Martian A* engine and auditable White-Box physics operate over Mars's true 3,396.19 km equatorial radius to model Pandolf metabolic oxygen depletion for NASA's xEMU spacesuit, enforce the sacred 30% emergency O2 reserve, block lethal >20° slopes, and verify UHF radio line-of-sight to shelter. With real-time solar storm emergency rerouting, Perseverance point-of-view panoramas, PIXL mineral targeting, printable wrist Cuff Cards, and 3D-printable (.STL) terrain, NEXO-ARES brings astronauts—and their science—home alive.
details:
LIVE INTERACTIVE SYSTEM & OPEN-SOURCE REPOSITORY

- Live EVA Survival Console: https://ortiz10m.github.io/nexo-code-nass/frontend/

- Source Code (MIT License): https://github.com/ortiz10m/nexo-code-nass

1. WHAT NEXO-ARES DOES & WHY IT IS HYPERLOCALIZED

While orbital portals like NASA Mars Trek excel at global and regional mapping, human explorers stepping onto Mars require hyperlocalized, meter-scale intelligence to survive individual Marswalks (EVAs). Mars has no GPS constellation, no breathable atmosphere, and lethal terrain traps—proven by Ingenuity's Flight 72 crash on featureless sand ripples and Spirit's entrapment in soft regolith.

NEXO-ARES is an integrated, multi-layered Martian survival and astrobiology mission planner focused specifically on Jezero Crater. Directly answering the challenge prompt, it unites two operational interfaces in one seamless platform:

1) A Habitat Mission Planning Console to design multi-stop routes across 13 real Jezero geological sites before stepping outside.

2) A 360° Augmented-Reality Helmet Visor HUD featuring authentic point-of-view Martian surface panoramas so astronauts know exactly what terrain, hazards, and science targets await at every destination.

2. HOW IT WORKS (ARCHITECTURE & WHITE-BOX PHYSICS ENGINE)

Because Martian surface crews cannot rely on continuous cloud connectivity, NEXO-ARES runs on a hybrid Offline-First architecture (Python FastAPI scientific core paired with a zero-latency JavaScript mirror engine in the suit browser, initializing in standard NASA English with an instant EN | ES bilingual toggle):

- Multi-Mission Layer Fusion: Integrates orbital orthoimagery (Mars Trek WMTS, JPL PIA24096, HiRISE), laser/stereo elevation (NASA MOLA + ESA HRSC), surface radiation baselines (Curiosity RAD: 0.028 mSv/h), and space-weather alerts (NASA DONKI SEP).

- Martian A* Pathfinding & Geodesy: Computes optimal traverses over Mars's true equatorial geodesic radius (3,396.19 km), dynamically adjusting survival range rings between Foot EVA and Pressurized Rover support.

- 100% Auditable White-Box Physics: Eliminates opaque black-box guesswork by solving four simultaneous survival equations at every step: (1) Geodesic distance and elevation gain, (2) Pandolf metabolic energy and oxygen expenditure under 0.38g Martian gravity for NASA's xEMU spacesuit, (3) Strict enforcement of NASA's 30% Bingo O2 emergency reserve, and (4) >20° steep-slope NO-GO barriers plus UHF radio horizon line-of-sight to Octavia E. Butler Base.

- Live Chaos Fault Simulator: Injects real-time mid-EVA contingencies—such as Solar Energetic Particle (SEP) radiation storms or sudden -35% O2 tank leaks—automatically dropping secondary waypoints in milliseconds to compute the fastest life-saving abort vector back to shelter.

3. KEY SURVIVAL & SCIENTIFIC BENEFITS

- Keeps Human Explorers Alive: Prevents metabolic exhaustion, steep crater wall slips (e.g., Belva Crater at 21.8°), UHF communication blackouts, and acute solar radiation exposure.

- Maximizes High-Value Astrobiology: Guides astronauts safely to prime biosignature-bearing outcrops (Maaz, Seitah, Neretva Vallis Delta) and Perseverance's Three Forks sample depot, while simulating hands-free PIXL/SuperCam mineral readouts (carbonates, olivine, sulfates) inside the 360° visor.

- Zero-Power Physical Backups: Generates printable Apollo/Artemis-style wrist Cuff Cards (with compass bearings and Bingo O2 thresholds) and exports 3D-printable (.STL) Jezero Crater terrain meshes.

4. WHAT WE HOPE TO ACHIEVE

We aim to demonstrate how multi-mission NASA and partner agency orbital/surface datasets can be fused into an actionable, human-centered EVA survival standard—bridging the gap between orbital planetary cartography and real-time human safety during future Mars surface science expeditions.

5. TOOLS, LANGUAGES & SOFTWARE USED

- Backend & Physics Core: Python 3, FastAPI, custom Martian spherical/geodesic A* pathfinding, Pandolf 0.38g metabolic equations, and NASA DONKI REST API integration.

- Frontend & 3D/AR Visualization: HTML5, CSS3 tactical HUD design, Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+ offline engine & i18n EN/ES support), Leaflet.js (Canvas-accelerated 2D multi-layer GIS), Three.js / WebGL (3D orbital landing context & 360° point-of-view AR helmet visor), Web Audio API (procedural suit breathing & comms telemetry), and client-side binary .STL mesh generation.

- Version Control & Hosting: Git, GitHub, and GitHub Pages.

AI TRANSPARENCY DISCLOSURE

In compliance with NASA Space Apps rules, generative AI (LLMs) assisted with UI/CSS HUD scaffolding, rapid code syntax generation, debugging, and English technical copyediting. All system architecture, Offline-First engineering, White-Box physical/biomedical equations, astrobiological site curation, and dataset verifications were conceived, directed, and validated by Team Nexo Code. Zero NASA logos, insignias, or restricted identifiers were used in AI tools.
